title: Stratified mini-evals for batching/cache safety
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Automatic batching and prefix/KV caching recommendations reduce per-token cost but can subtly change model outputs for tail prompt cohorts. Current autotune runs suggest ~12-18% token savings on high-throughput endpoints, but product teams raised concerns about micro-regressions for billing-sensitive customers and high-precision flows (summarization, financial copy).

Goal: Build a compact, traffic-aware mini-eval harness that stratifies live traffic into cohorts, runs targeted golden-prompt + cohort probes, computes lightweight behavioral metrics (embedding drift, top-k token divergence, and latency-weighted quality delta), and produces deterministic acceptance signals for safe config apply and automated rollback. This ticket delivers the evaluation harness, acceptance thresholds, rollout gating logic, and integration points for the apply/orchestrator service.

Approach:
- Create a stratified sampling module that derives 8 representative cohorts from production logs (e.g., short-chat, long-chat, instruction-completion, code, reranking, conversational stateful, legal/finance, embeddings-adjacent prompts). Cohorts are updated weekly to reflect traffic shifts.
- For each proposed batching/cache config, run a parallel mini-eval where 250 cohort-specific golden prompts are executed against baseline config and candidate config in shadow mode.
- Compute three primary signals per cohort: (1) semantic cosine drift using 3k-dim embeddings (candidate vs baseline mean cosine >= -0.015 allowed), (2) token-distribution JS divergence on top-50 tokens (must be <= 0.02), (3) latency P95 change (<= +10% absolute). An overall cohort pass requires all three signals to be within thresholds and no decrease in human-reviewed fidelity on sampled anchors.
- Compose cohort passes into a global acceptance rule using weighted aggregation (weights derived from cohort traffic share + customer_sensitivity flag). Default global acceptance requires >= 90% weighted pass rate.
- If any cohort fails, the system flags the config and surfaces targeted diffs (example outputs, embeddings, token-delta histograms) to engineers and to the human audit queue.

Rollout plan / automation:
- Phase A (manual): Evaluate harness results and human-audit for a small set of internal endpoints (2 teams).
- Phase B (shadow apply): Integrate with autotune recommendation engine to run the mini-eval for all candidate configs before generating apply tickets. No config changes applied yet; results stored in console and linked PRs.
- Phase C (canary): If harness passes, allow a 1% canary apply with enhanced telemetry and golden-prompt checks every hour. Automated rollback triggers defined below.
- Phase D (ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% based on periodic re-evaluation (every 12h) and continuous checks.

Automated rollback triggers:
- Any cohort-level embedding drift > 0.03 OR JS divergence > 0.05 triggers immediate rollback.
- Global weighted pass rate drops below 75% for two consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Production SLA latency impact exceeds +25% P95 for 30 minutes.
- Any customer-facing alerts tagged "sensitive-output" are fired by downstream monitors.

Outputs delivered:
- Mini-eval harness service (k8s job + lightweight runner) that accepts candidate config tarball and baseline tag.
- Console dashboard with cohort breakdown, histograms, scatterplots of embedding deltas, example diffs, and automatic suggestions for more conservative cache/batch parameters when borderline.
- API endpoint for the orchestrator to request an acceptance decision for a candidate config.

Metrics to monitor:
- False positive rate of harness (human-audited regressions missed) < 2% after first month.
- Average time to evaluate a candidate config for a top-traffic model: <= 18 minutes.
- Number of automated rollbacks per 100 applies: target < 1 after stabilization.

Longer-term: integrate with cost advisor to recommend adjusted thresholds per-customer, and add human-in-the-loop tagging to expand the golden prompt corpus for underrepresented cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute end-to-end for a candidate config within 20 minutes for a production model (measured on CI using 8-cohort sample)
Cohort stratifier code committed with tests and weekly cohort refresh job scheduled
Console pages show per-cohort signals, example diffs, and a clear accept/reject decision for every run
Orchestrator API accepts candidate config, returns pass/fail and structured reasons; automated canary uses this API before apply
Automated rollback triggers implemented and validated in staging with synthetic failures
Documentation and runbook for human auditors (how to triage flagged diffs) published in Confluence
